belief: God is like my father (or mother).
meta: A Christian look at the false belief that God is like your earthly father or mother, with Scripture, questions, and homework for replacing it with the truth.
origins: Childhood experiences with a parent who was harsh, distant, critical, absent, unpredictable, or abusive. Learning about God mainly through how your parents treated you. Hearing God called “Father” and feeling fear, anger, or emptiness instead of comfort. Even loving parents are imperfect, and their weaknesses can shape how we picture God.
teaches: Earthly parents, even good ones, are imperfect. God is the perfect Father. Jesus said that if imperfect parents know how to give good gifts, how much more will your Father in heaven give good things to those who ask. God is a father to the fatherless, has compassion on His children, and leads with cords of kindness. Even if a mother could forget her child, God will not forget you. Though father and mother forsake you, the LORD will receive you.
self_statements: God is distant, just like my dad was.
God is always angry, like my father.
God is never satisfied, like my mother.
God will leave, like my parent did.
I can’t trust God because I couldn’t trust my parents.
God is unpredictable, like the people who raised me.
errors: Assuming God has the same faults as your parents.
Turning one relationship into a picture of every father, including God.
Concluding “God feels like my parent, so He must be like my parent.”
Ignoring what Scripture says about God’s character.
questions: In what ways do I picture God like my father or mother?
What does Matthew 7:11 say about how much better God is than earthly parents?
What does Psalm 27:10 promise if my parents forsook me?
Is my picture of God coming from Scripture or from my childhood?
What qualities of God in Scripture are different from my parents?
Can I grieve what my parents didn’t give me and still receive it from God?
What would it be like to have a perfect Father?
truth: God is not like my father or mother. Earthly parents are imperfect; God is the perfect Father. He is compassionate, kind, faithful, and never forgets me. Even if my parents failed or forsook me, the LORD receives me. I can let Scripture, not my childhood, show me who God really is.
hw_questions: How do I picture God like my parent?
How much better is God than earthly parents?
What does God promise if my parents forsook me?
Is my picture of God from Scripture or childhood?
How is God different from my parents?
What would a perfect Father be like?
hw_truths: Though my father and mother forsake me, the LORD will receive me.
God has compassion on me like a loving father.
God leads me with kindness and love.
My heavenly Father gives good things to me.
log: Each day, write one quality of God from Scripture and how it differs from my earthly parent.
name_example: Though Sarah’s father and mother forsake her, the LORD will receive her.

tracker: One way God is better than my parent
prayer: Heavenly Father, thank You that You are the perfect Father. Help me reject the lie that You are like my earthly father or mother. Heal the hurts my parents caused, and show me who You really are: compassionate, kind, faithful, and always present. Teach me to trust You as Your child. In Jesus’ name, Amen.

God’s faithful presence challenges the expectation of rejection and abandonment.
